events.description: Leaders of the Islamic State of Iraq, including Abu Ayyub al-Masri, killed, leading to premature declarations of AQI's defeat.
Resolute Support evacuated Afghan forces from Sangin district center, flattened it and relocated it four miles away, claiming government control.
Al-Qaeda in Iraq took Fallujah, Ramadi and most of western Anbar, then overran Mosul.
US raid on two large al-Qaeda camps in Shorabak district killed about 150-200 fighters, raising the estimate to 200.
Ghazni City fell to the Taliban; seven districts previously 'administered' from it were exposed as Taliban-controlled.
Taliban cut Route Bear, the critical supply node to Uruzgan.
Gen. Nicholson tells Sen. McCain the war is a stalemate and the Taliban gained ~15% territory since 2015.
General Razik met TAAC-South leadership in the dining facility during Ramadan.
General Razik killed by the Taliban (hosts unsure whether 2018 or 2019).
Taliban take Kandahar city and Kandahar Airfield, then Kabul, after Trump's deal and Biden's withdrawal.
Secretary of Defense Mattis stepped down because he could not execute Trump's decision to leave Syria.
Trump 'cut the deal' with the Taliban and Biden later executed the US exit from Afghanistan.
Obama surge in Afghanistan ended and Obama wanted to leave the country, after which the war 'became pointless'.

key_claims: Hosts argue official estimates of 50-100 al-Qaeda in Afghanistan were badly low; guests assessed roughly 300-400 in Kandahar and 200-300 in Uruzgan alone.
Intelligence on district control was manipulated upward by commanders, so districts were rated contested when under Taliban control.
The Taliban's rural-first guerrilla strategy, articulated by Mullah Amanullah, surrounded Uruzgan's capital and ultimately won the war.
General Razik was effective against the Taliban but corrupt, feuded with the Noorzai and fueled Taliban recruitment.
Cutting Route Bear in Oct 2016 isolated Uruzgan and showed that the US-Afghan hold was a 'paper tiger'.
The Trump deal and Biden withdrawal merely closed a defeat already evident by 2014-2019.
Al-Qaeda in Iraq was not defeated in 2010-11; it regrouped and rose as the Islamic State by 2014.
Lack of accountability and repeated analytic mistakes in Afghanistan risk recurrence in Ukraine.
US forces rotating National Guard units were placed in roles they were not trained or given time to prepare for, because the military was overstretched by Iraq.
The first National Guard rotation made progress by strengthening ANSF and Afghan special forces, while the second pursued kills over sustained mission goals.
Lack of continuity from commander to commander undermined US missions in Iraq and Afghanistan.
The State Department never built up the Afghan government, leaving military officers to handle civil tasks like water disputes.
The war 'became pointless' after the surge ended and Obama sought to leave, followed by Trump's deal and Biden's execution of the withdrawal.
Low US casualties and few political families serving reduced pressure to end or win the war.
